candidate_draft.description_long: On October 25, 1968, The Guardian reported that effective control of the News of the World was passing to Australia's News Ltd. The article said News Ltd. was to take a 40% stake, described as the largest single holding, in a deal intended to defeat a takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell. It also reported that Rupert Murdoch, then News Ltd.'s chairman, was to become joint managing director alongside the newspaper's current chairman, Sir William Carr. These are the terms and management changes described in a contemporary report; its wording describes what was to happen and does not independently confirm completion of the transaction. The source documents a British newspaper ownership dispute. It does not mention Donald Trump, and the linked TrumpFile page concerns different newspaper titles. A source or editorial rationale connecting this transaction to Trump-focused coverage is still needed before treating this factual correction as release-ready.

candidate_draft.description_long: In Burwell v. Hobby Lobby Stores, Inc., decided June 30, 2014, the Supreme Court considered challenges by closely held for-profit corporations to the Affordable Care Act's contraceptive-coverage requirement. The Court held that, as applied to closely held corporations, the HHS regulations imposing that mandate violated the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA). The official opinion discusses whether RFRA applies to those companies and the statutory burden at issue; it does not announce a general rule that corporations possess every right held by natural persons. The packet identifies the 2014 case but supplies no Trump statement, appointment, policy, or other action connected to the decision. A later Trump executive order, signed in May 2017, instructed Treasury, Labor, and HHS to consider amended regulations addressing conscience-based objections to the preventive-care mandate. That was a separate presidential act, not part of the Court's 2014 ruling. This narrowed description accurately states the case, but the item remains on hold for Trump coverage until an attributable Trump connection to the 2014 case or an explicit editorial scope for standalone court decisions is documented.
